headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from Khoj’s file-backed retrieval interacting with Taipy’s automation stack; no direct shared-channel evidence, so uncertainty stays elevated.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files and can use RAG plus optional web search, so malicious content in shared documents could be surfaced as instructions. Taipy is a data-engineering/automation framework, so if it consumes Khoj output without filtering, prompt injection is plausible. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF Taipy ingests Khoj-generated text as instructions or workflow parameters
IF both agents share a document store or exported notes folder
mitigations: Add an explicit instruction/content separator in Taipy inputs
Whitelist only structured fields from Khoj output
Disable automatic execution of text copied from notes
Review shared folders for untrusted note sources
requires-engineering: add provenance tags end-to-end

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents and has broad network egress, while Taipy is documented with no network egress. If they share files or a workspace, Khoj content could be exposed through Taipy workflows or logs. The pairwise leak path is inferred, not directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or exported files
IF Taipy logs or republishes data derived from Khoj notes
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Remove sensitive notes from any shared export path
Turn off verbose logging in Taipy workflows
Restrict Khoj indexing to non-sensitive collections
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Khoj can read the filesystem but cannot write it, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. Taipy has no documented write, git, or network capabilities in the profile. With no overlapping mutable write surface, direct capability conflict is limited and likely requires unusual orchestration.
conditions: IF Taipy is extended with filesystem or git write plugins
IF an external orchestrator grants both agents the same mutable resource
mitigations: Keep Taipy read-only for shared artifacts
Avoid mounting the same writable directory
Disable any git automation around the pair
Audit for hidden plugins or wrappers
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj can generate retrieved answers from notes and documents, and Taipy is tagged for automation/job scheduling. If Taipy treats Khoj output as authoritative, an error or hallucination can cascade into downstream workflows. Taipy’s lack of documented verification controls makes the interaction risky, though not clearly high-impact from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF Taipy uses Khoj output as a direct workflow input
IF no human or schema validation occurs before Taipy acts
mitigations: Require schema validation before Taipy consumes outputs
Insert a human review step for high-impact actions
Limit Taipy to read-only reporting from Khoj
Log source citations alongside every derived field
requires-engineering: add confidence gating before automation

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj explicitly touches personal notes and indexed documents, which can carry privacy obligations, while Taipy’s profile does not show regulated-data handling or residency commitments. The main compliance concern is local privacy/process mismatch rather than a documented cross-border or certification conflict, so low is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF personal notes include regulated data classes
IF Taipy stores or logs derived note content without a retention policy
mitigations: Classify note collections before indexing
Exclude regulated notes from Khoj
Set a short log-retention window in Taipy
Document data-handling responsibilities
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows
